en: Taal Volcano features Vulcan Point, a tiny island containing a crater lake situated inside the main crater of Volcano Island inside Lake Taal.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park features an eight-kilometer underground river that flows directly into the West Philippine Sea.
Mount Pulag, the highest peak in Luzon, experiences freezing temperatures that occasionally drop below zero degrees Celsius during the winter months.
Bohol's Chocolate Hills consist of over one thousand cone-shaped karst limestone mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a UNESCO World Heritage site protecting over six hundred marine species.
The Philippines sits at the epicenter of the Coral Triangle, which contains the highest marine biodiversity of any region on Earth.
Lake Mainit in Surigao del Norte is the deepest lake in the Philippines, reaching a maximum depth of over two hundred meters.
Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for its remarkably perfect symmetrical cone shape, formed by layers of solidified lava and volcanic ash.
The island province of Camiguin is unique because it contains seven volcanoes, which is more than the number of its municipalities.
The Philippines experiences two primary monsoon winds, the southwest Habagat bringing heavy rains and the cool, dry northeast Amihan.
The Philippines holds the world's largest known copper and gold deposits and is among the top global producers of nickel.
The Hinatuan Enchanted River in Surigao del Sur features mysteriously deep, crystal-clear blue water that flows directly from underground mountain springs.
